title: Grateful Dead Live at Hollywood Palladium on 1971-08-06
source: Lineage: MAR (Harvey Kaslow) @ 7 1/2 ips. > R @ 7 1/2 ips.(Don Wolfe); Transfer info:  Akai GX636 direct tape head output  > Bottlehead tube tape pre pair Tesla tubes circa 1980  > Apogee Mini Me 24/96  > Apogee Mini DAC monitoring and mastering  > FLAC

ai_review.summary: A phenomenal 1971 show captured on an audience recording that delivers high‑energy “bounce” and a standout Me & Bobby McGee performance.
ai_review.review: Both reviewers rave about the musical fire of this late‑summer ’71 concert – calling it a zenith of the Pigpen era with every song “bouncing”. The audience tape is praised for its surprisingly clear balance (a “Goldilocks” spot in the venue), making the recording enjoyable despite being an older‑sounding source. Overall, the performance and sound combine to give a very positive listening experience.

ai_rating.rationale: Two detailed reviews rate the show 4–5 stars, praising both musical energy and recording clarity; weighting favors the strong performance, yielding a high overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Audience tape is described as well‑balanced, clear enough to be called a “Goldilocks” recording; not pristine soundboard quality but far better than typical audience sources of the era.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows with relentless energy, described as a “bounce” throughout; reviewers note it feels like a high point of the Pigpen era.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Mentioned for his solos (differences noted compared to later shows) and overall strong guitar work.
